label: prop:rr0-comparison
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The implication \ref{it:rr0-comp-pos}$\Rightarrow$\ref{it:rr0-comp-proj} is clear.  Conversely, suppose \ref{it:rr0-comp-proj} holds.
    By replacing $A$ with $M_n(A)$, it suffices to show that if $a, b \in A_+$ and $d_\tau(a) < d_\tau(b)$ for all $\tau \in X$, then $a \precsim b$.  
    By \cite[Theorem 5]{CEI},\footnote{Although this result states that $A$ has stable rank one, the proof that real rank zero implies every element is the supremum of classes of projections does not use this hypothesis.} there exist projections $p_i,q_i$ such that $[a]=\sup_i [p_i]$ and $[b]=\sup_i [q_i]$, with the sequences increasing.
    For each $i$, since $\tau(p_i) < d_\tau(a)$ for all $\tau\in X$, by lower semicontinuity and compactness, there exists $\epsilon>0$ such that $\tau(p_i)+\epsilon<d_\tau(a)$ for all $\tau \in X$.
    Then since $d_\tau(a) = \sup_j \tau(q_j)$, by Dini's Theorem, there exists $j$ such that $\tau(p_i) +\epsilon < \tau(q_j)$ for all $\tau \in X$.
    Applying comparison of projections, we have $[p_i] \leq [q_j] \leq [b]$.
    Since $i$ is arbitrary, we may conclude $[a]\leq[b]$.

label: lem:aff-lift-valuesp
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:aff-lift-valuesp}
    Let $X$ be a Choquet simplex, $Y$ be a closed face of $X$, and let $F$ be a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra.  Every continuous affine map $\alpha\colon Y\to T(F)$ admits an extension to a continuous affine map $\beta\colon X\to T(F)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $F=\oplus_{k=1}^mM_{n_k}$ and let $\alpha\colon Y \rightarrow T(F)$ be given. Then we can decompose $\alpha$ as a sum $\sum_{k=1}^m \alpha_k \mathrm{tr}_{n_k}$, where $\mathrm{tr}_{n_k}$ is the normalised trace on $M_{n_k}$ and for each $k=1,2,\hdots,m$,  $\alpha_k\colon Y\rightarrow [0,1]$ is a continuous affine function such that $\sum_{k=1}^m \alpha_k=1$.
    Inductively, for each $k=1,\dots,m-1$, using Corollary~\ref{cor:extending-affine-2}, we may find $\beta_k \in \operatorname{{Aff}}(X)_+$ such that $\beta_k|_Y=\alpha_k$ and $\beta_k \leq 1-(\beta_1+\cdots+\beta_{k-1})$. 
    Then set $\beta_m\coloneqq 1-(\beta_1+\cdots+\beta_{m-1})$, which will automatically satisfy $\beta_m|_Y=\alpha_m$, and finally set $\beta\coloneqq \sum_{k=1}^m \beta_k \mathrm{tr}_{n_k}$.

label: 2909_rem_amplification
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{2909_rem_amplification}
    In a couple of places in this paper, we will make use of matrix amplifications of tracially complete $C^*$-algebras. Given a tracially complete $C^*$-algebra $(\mathcal{M}, X)$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, we identify $M_n \otimes \mathcal{M}$ and $M_n(\mathcal{M})$ in the usual way and write $X_n$ for the set of traces on $M_n(\mathcal{M})$ of the form $\mathrm{tr}_n \otimes \tau$ where $\tau \in X$. Then $(M_n(\mathcal{M}), X_n)$ is a tracially complete $C^*$-algebra. (Indeed, this is a special case of tensor products; see \cite[Section 3.5]{carrion2023tracially}.) Since $\mathrm{tr}_n$ is the normalised trace on $M_n$, we have that $\|x\|_{2,X} = \sqrt{n}\|x \oplus 0_{n-1}\|_{2,X_n}$ for all $x \in \mathcal{M}$ where we view $\mathcal{M} \subseteq M_n(\mathcal{M})$ by embedding $\mathcal{M}$ in the top left corner.

label: prop:tracial-ultrapower-is-TC
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:tracial-ultrapower-is-TC}
    Let $A$ be a $C^*$-algebra with $T(A)$ non-empty and compact. 
    Let $(\mathcal{M},X)$ be the tracial completion of $A$ with respect to $T(A)$.
    Then canonical map $A \rightarrow \mathcal{M}$ induces an isomorphism $(A^\omega, \overline{T_\omega(A)}) \cong (\mathcal{M}^\omega, X^\omega)$.
    In particular, $A^\omega$ is unital and $(A^\omega, \overline{T_\omega(A)})$ is a tracially complete $C^*$-algebra.
head: environment

label: strict_compa_A_ultrap
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Note that since $T(A)$ is compact, $A^\omega$ is unital, and so $\overline{T_\omega(A)}$ is a compact subset of $T(A^\omega)$. It is standard that the norm ultrapower $A_\omega$ has strict comparison with respect to $\overline{T_\omega(A)}$ (see \cite[Lemma 1.23]{BBSTWW}, which only uses the unitality assumption through the compactness of $\overline{T_\omega(A)}$). This passes to the quotient $A^\omega$.\footnote{If $a,b\in M_n(A^\omega)_+$ have $d_\tau(a)<d_\tau(b)$ for all $\tau\in \overline{T_\omega(A)}$, then  positive lifts $\tilde{a},\tilde{b}\in M_n(A_\omega)_+$ and abusing notation to regard ($T_\omega(A)$ as traces on $A_\omega$) will have $d_\tau(\tilde{a})<d_\tau(\tilde{b})$ for all $\tau\in\overline{T_\omega(A)}$. Strict comparison of $A_\omega$ with respect to $\overline{T_\omega(A)}$ gives $\tilde{a}\precsim \tilde{b}$ in $A_\omega$, and hence $a\precsim b$ in $A^\omega$.}  Then $T(A^\omega)=\overline{T_\omega(A)}$ is a consequence of Proposition~\ref{prop:computing-traces}.
    The second part follows from applying the first part to $A=\mathcal{M}$, which will have $T(\mathcal{M})=X$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:computing-traces}, and hence $X^\omega=\overline{T_\omega(\mathcal{M})}$.   
    The fact that $T(A^\omega)=\overline{T_\omega(A)}$ is a consequence of Proposition~\ref{prop:computing-traces}.

label: lem:trace-trick
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: cf.\

title: Remark
body_md:
We shall typically suppress the details of our applications of Kirchberg's epsilon test. Many examples can be found in the literature (particularly in \cite{BBSTWW}). For an example application in the tracially complete framework, see \cite[Lemma 5.4]{carrion2023tracially}.   However, we would like to make a crucial observation. The output of Kirchberg's epsilon test when working with tracial ultrapowers will always be estimates that hold for all \emph{limit traces}, and then by continuity for the closure of this set as well. If $T(A^\omega)$ contains traces not in $\overline{T(A_\omega)}$ this argument says nothing about those traces (notwithstanding that a positive element that vanishes on $T_\omega(A)$ is zero in the tracial ultrapower).
    In our applications we will typically use the last part of Proposition~\ref{strict_compa_A_ultrap} ensuring that there are no such traces.

For a self-adjoint $b\in\mathcal{M}$ with $\|b\|\leq\|g\|_\infty$ which realises $g$, we have $a\coloneqq b+\|f\|_\infty/2\geq 0$ (recalling that $\mathcal{M}$ is unital) has $\|a\|\leq\|f\|_\infty$ and $a$ realises $f$.

title: Remark
body_md:
We note that the hypotheses that $(\mathcal{M},X)$ is type II$_1$ and factorial are 
    is redundant under the assumptions that $\mathcal{M}^\omega$ has strict comparison with respect to $X^\omega$ and $\mathcal{M}^\omega$ has a divisible unit. 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Divisibility of the unit and order zero lifting give order zero maps $M_n\to\mathcal{M}$ which are not contained in the kernel of any $\pi_\tau$ for all $\tau \in X$. Accordingly, each $\pi_\tau(\mathcal{M})''$ is type II$_1$.
        \item Strict comparison of $\mathcal{M}^\omega$ with with respect to $X^\omega$ implies $T(\mathcal{M}^\omega)=X^\omega$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:computing-traces}.
        Suppose $\sigma\in T(\mathcal{M})$ is in the face generated by $X$.  Then there is a constant $C > 0$ and a trace $\tau \in X$ such that $\tau \leq C\sigma$, and in particular, $\sigma$ is $\|\cdot\|_{2, X}$-continuous.
        Then the limit trace $\sigma_\omega$ given by just using $\sigma$ is in $T(\mathcal{M}^\omega)=X^\omega$.
        The continuous affine map $T(\mathcal{M}^\omega) \rightarrow T(\mathcal{M})$ given by $\tau \mapsto \tau|_\mathcal{M}$ maps $X^\omega$ into $X$ since $X$ is closed.
        Therefore, $\sigma = \sigma_\omega|_\mathcal{M} \in X$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Nevertheless, we will include the type II$_1$ and factorial hypotheses in the statements of results in this section in accordance with Definition~\ref{def:classification-of-projections}.

label: Cor:FakeSpectralProjection
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{Cor:FakeSpectralProjection} 
Let $(\mathcal{M},X)$ be a II$_1$ factorial tracially complete $C^*$-algebra such that $\mathcal M^\omega$ has strict comparison with respect to $X^\omega$ and $\mathcal{M}^\omega$ has a divisible unit. 
Let $F\subseteq \mathcal{M}^{\omega}$ be a finite-dimensional subalgebra. 
For $b\in\mathcal{M}^\omega_+ \cap F'$ with and $\delta>0$, there exists a projection $q\in\mathcal{M}^\omega \cap F' \cap \{b\}'$ such that $qb\leq \delta q$ and $(1-q)b\geq \delta (1-q)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $\epsilon>0$. Since $\mathcal{M}^\omega$ has real rank zero by Proposition \ref{S4.2:Prop}(ii), $\mathcal{M}^{\omega}\cap F'$ also has real rank zero by Lemma~\ref{Lem:RelCom} (we may assume that $F$ contains the unit to apply this, since unitising $F$ does not change the commutant). 
    Then there exists a finite spectrum element $c\in \mathcal{M}^\omega \cap F'$ with $\|c-b\|< \epsilon$. Let $q \in \mathcal{M}^\omega \cap F'$ be the spectral projection of $c$ for $[0,\delta]$ so that $qc = cq$,  $qc\leq \delta q$ and $(1-q)c\geq \delta(1-q)$. Then $\|[q, b]\| < 2 \epsilon$, $qbq\leq(\delta+\epsilon)q$, and $(1-q)b(1-q)\geq (\delta+\epsilon)(1-q)$. The result follows from Kirchberg's epsilon test.

label: 2609_Aloweromega_kstable
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{2609_Aloweromega_kstable} 
    Let $A$ be a unital $C^*$-algebra with $T(A)\neq \emptyset$. 
    Suppose $A$ has strict comparison with respect to $T(A)$ and $[1_A]\in \mathrm{Cu}(A)$ is almost divisible. 
    Then $A^\omega$ is $K$-stable.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(\mathcal{M}, X)$ be the tracial completion of $A$ with respect to $T(A)$. 
By Proposition \ref{prop:tracial-ultrapower-is-TC}, we have $(A^{\omega}, \overline{T_{\omega}(A)}) \cong (\mathcal{M}^{\omega}, X^{\omega})$.
Hence, by Proposition \ref{prop:sc_divisible_tracial_ultra}, our strict comparison and almost divisibility hypotheses on $A$ imply that $\mathcal{M}^{\omega}$ has strict comparison with respect to $X^{\omega}$ and $\mathcal{M}^{\omega}$ has a divisible unit. 
Therefore, $\mathcal{M}^{\omega}$ has stable rank one by Proposition~\ref{S4.2:Prop} and has divisibility in the sense of Rieffel (see \cite[Definition~4.1]{rieffel87}).  
Combining these results with \cite[Theorem 4.13]{rieffel87} gives $K$-stability of $\mathcal{M}^{\omega}$. Hence, $A^{\omega}$ is $K$-stable.
head: environment

label: prop:J_A_K_stable
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:J_A_K_stable}
Let $A$ be a unital $C^*$-algebra with $T(A) \neq \emptyset$. Suppose that $A$ has strict comparison with respect to $T(A)$. Then $J_{A}$ is $K$-stable.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the proof of \cite[Lemma 6.11]{CGSTW},\footnote{The argument in \cite{CGSTW} has additional assumptions: simplicity and $\mathcal{Z}$-stability, but in fact only relies on $A_{\omega}$ having strict comparison with respect to $\overline{T_\omega(A)}$ which follows from strict comparison of $A$ with respect to $T(A)$; see \cite[Lemma 1.23]{BBSTWW}. See the discussion of hypotheses in \cite[Section 1.3.6]{CGSTW}.} since $A$ has strict comparison with respect to $T(A)$, the trace-kernel ideal $J_A$ is separably stable. Fix $k \geq 0$ and $n\geq 1$. 
We show injectivity of $\pi_{k}(i_{n, n+1})$ and surjectivity follows from a similar strategy. 

To prove injectivity of $\pi_{k}(i_{n, n+1})$, take a continuous function $f: S^{k}\rightarrow \mathcal{V}_{n}(J_{A})$ such that $i_{n, n+1} \circ f$ is homotopic to the constant function $1_{n+1}$. 
Let $F: [0,1]\times S^{k}\rightarrow \mathcal{V}_{n+1}(J_{A})$ be the homotopy. 
Then matrix entries of $f(x) - 1_{n}$ and $F(y) - 1_{n+1}$ for $x\in S^{k}$ and $y\in [0,1]\times S^{k}$ generate a separable $C^*$-subalgebra as $S^{k}$ is compact and metrisable. This is contained in a separable stable subalgebra $B\subseteq J_{B}$ by separable stability. As $B$ is stable, it is $K$-stable. By the definition of $B$, we can view $f$ as a map into $\mathcal{V}_{n}(B)$ such that $i_{n, n+1}\circ f$ is homotopic to $1_{n+1}$ in $\mathcal{V}_{n+1}(B)$. The $K$-stability of $B$ implies that $f$ is homotopic to $1_{n}$ in $\mathcal{V}_{n}(B)$. Hence, $f$ is homotopic to $1_{n}$ in $\mathcal{V}_{n}(J_A)$).

It is in establishing the claim in the proof of Theorem~\ref{SmallLocalApproximations} where we use that the elements given by weak CPoU form a partition of unity which is morally subordinate to the given convex open cover.  The main difficulty is bounding $\tau(q)$ from below, which splits into cases according to whether or not $\tau (e_{n}) < \beta$
for a small value $\beta$. This should be compared with the more classical partition of unity argument in the sketch proof of Lemma~\ref{RobotLemma} in Section~\ref{RobotSection}, where the corresponding lower bound comes from separately considering $\tau(f_n)$ for $\tau\in U_n$, and that $f_n$ is supported $U_n$.  In both cases, this gives enough space to obtain the required projection via the classification of projections.

body_md:
\label{PureAmenable=>Hyperfinite}	
Let $(\mathcal M, X)$ be a II$_1$ factorial amenable tracially complete $C^*$-algebra such that $\mathcal M^\omega$ has strict comparison with respect to $X^\omega$ and $\mathcal M^\omega$ has divisible unit.  Then $(\mathcal M,X)$ is hyperfinite.

body_md:
The equivalence of \ref{TC:Structure:MainBody.1}, \ref{TC:Structure:MainBody.2}, \ref{TC:Structure:MainBody.2'},
    and \ref{TC:Structure:MainBody.2''} is \cite[Theorem~9.15]{carrion2023tracially}.
    The implication \ref{TC:Structure:MainBody.2''}$\Rightarrow$\ref{TC:Structure:MainBody.3} holds without the amenability assumption. This is the combination of \cite[Proposition 7.2]{carrion2023tracially} (which shows $\mathcal{M}^\omega$ has real rank zero), \cite[Proposition 7.4]{carrion2023tracially} (comparison of projections in $(\mathcal{M}^\omega,X^\omega)$), and \cite[Theorem 7.18]{carrion2023tracially} (existence of projections from CPoU, which applies to $(\mathcal{M}^\omega,X^\omega)$ as this inherits CPoU from $\mathcal{M}$ by \cite[Corollary 7.7(i)]{carrion2023tracially}).\footnote{The authors of \cite{carrion2023tracially} neglected to explicitly collect the existence of projections in $\mathcal{M}^\omega$ when $(\mathcal{M},X)$ has CPoU, focusing instead on the existence of projections in $(\mathcal{M},X)$.}   Then classification of projections in $\mathcal M^\omega$ implies the classification of finite-dimensional subalgebras by Proposition~\ref{Class:FD}, which in turn implies $\mathcal M^\omega$ has divisible unit.  Then Proposition~\ref{prop:rr0-comparison} implies $\mathcal M^\omega$ has strict comparison with respect to $X^\omega$. 
    The final piece is \ref{TC:Structure:MainBody.3}$\Rightarrow$\ref{TC:Structure:MainBody.1}, which we have just established in Theorem \ref{PureAmenable=>Hyperfinite}.

label: lem:reduction-a-la-brown
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We note that the following properties are invariant under stable isomorphism: stable finiteness, simplicity, separability, nuclearity and $\mathcal{Z}$-stability. (The latter is \cite[Section 3]{TomsWinter:TAMS} and the rest are standard; see \cite[Proposition 2.3]{CE:APDE} and the references therein for an overview). 
    Pureness is also invariant under stable isomorphism because it is a property of the Cuntz semigroup, which is by definition a stable isomorphism invariant.
    We will construct $B$ such that $T(B)$ is compact and all densely-defined lower-semicontinuous traces on $B$ are bounded.
    By pureness, it then follows that $B$ has strict comparison with respect to $T(B)$.
    
    There are two cases to consider: either $A \otimes \mathcal{K}$ contains a non-zero projection or it does not.
    
    First, suppose there is a non-zero projection $p \in A \otimes \mathcal{K}$. 
    Set $B = p(A \otimes \mathcal{K})p$.
    Clearly both $B$ and $A\otimes\mathcal{K}$ are separable, so have strictly positive elements. 
    As $A$ is simple, so is $A \otimes \mathcal{K}$; hence, $B$ is a full hereditary subalgebra of $A \otimes \mathcal{K}$. 
    Therefore, by Brown's theorem \cite[Theorem 2.8]{Brown:PJM}, $B$ is stably isomorphic to $A$.
    Clearly, $B$ is unital (with unit $p$). 
    Since $B$ is simple and unital, all densely-defined lower-semicontinuous traces on $B$ are bounded, so up to scaling they are tracial states. 
    Since $B$ is unital stably finite and exact, $T(B)$ is non-empty by \cite{BH82} and \cite{Haagerup}.
    As $B$ is unital, $T(B)$ is compact.
    
    Second, suppose $A \otimes \mathcal{K}$ contains no non-zero projections (i.e.\ $A$ is stably projectionless). By \cite[Lemma 3.3]{CE:PAMS}, which is also a hereditary subalgebra argument using Brown's theorem, there exists a $C^*$-algebra $B$ such that $B$ is stably isomorphic to $A$ such that all densely-defined lower-semicontinuous traces on $B$ are bounded and the trace space $T(B)$ is both non-empty and compact.

label: thm:McDuff1again
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:McDuff1again}
    Let $A$ be a separable and nuclear $C^*$-algebra such that $T(A)$ is compact and non-empty.  Suppose that $A$ has strict comparison with respect to $T(A)$ and an almost divisible strictly positive element.  Then its tracial completion $(\overline{A}{}^{T(A)},T(A))$ is McDuff.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let $(\mathcal{M},X) = (\overline{A}{}^{T(A)},T(A))$ be the tracial completion of $A$. Then $\mathcal{M}$ is factorial by \cite[Proposition 3.23(iv)]{carrion2023tracially}. Moreover, $\mathcal{M}$ is amenable by \cite[Corollary 4.10]{carrion2023tracially}.\footnote{Note that this is really Connes' theorem, as the content is that each $\pi_\tau(A)''$ is an amenable von Neumann algebra.}  Applying Proposition~\ref{prop:sc_divisible_tracial_ultra} and Proposition \ref{prop:tracial-ultrapower-is-TC}, we see that $\mathcal{M}^\omega$ has strict comparison with respect to $X^\omega$ and has a divisible unit. By Corollary \ref{TC:Structure:MainBody} (iii)$\Rightarrow$(ii), $\mathcal{M}$ is McDuff.

label: Intro-body:ThmA
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Intro-body:ThmA}
    Let $A$ be a simple separable nuclear pure $C^*$-algebra.  Then $A$ is $\mathcal Z$-stable.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $A$ be a simple separable nuclear pure $C^*$-algebra. Then $A$ is exact, and so all lower-semicontinuous densely-defined quasitraces on $A \otimes \mathcal{K}$ are additive by Haagerup's theorem; see \cite{Haagerup} for the unital case and \cite[Remark 2.29(i)]{BlanchardKirchberg:JFA} for the non-unital version. If $A$ is traceless, then $A$ is a Kirchberg algebra,\footnote{This is well known, as when $T(A)=\emptyset$ we have $a\precsim b$ for all non-zero $a,b\in A$, and hence $A$ is simple and purely infinite} so is $\mathcal O_\infty$-stable by Kirchberg's $\mathcal O_\infty$-absorption theorem (\cite{K:ICM,KP:Crelle}), and finally $\mathcal{Z}$-stable as $\mathcal O_\infty$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable (by the Kirchberg--Phillips theorem, for example).
    
    Hence, we may assume that $A$ is stably finite. 
    By Lemma~\ref{lem:reduction-a-la-brown}, we may further that $T(A)$ is compact and $A$ has strict comparison with respect to $T(A)$ (without affecting the stable isomorphism class of $A$). Since $A$ is separable, it has a strictly positive element $h \in A_+$. As $A$ is pure, $h$ is almost divisible.
    Then by Theorem~\ref{thm:McDuff1again},  $A$ has the uniform McDuff property. In the unital case, $\mathcal{Z}$-stability of $A$ now follows by Matui--Sato's $\mathcal{Z}$-stability theorem (see for example \cite[Theorem 2.6]{TWW:IMRN}). In the non-unital case, we need to use an appropriate non-unital version of Matui and Sato's $\mathcal{Z}$-stability theorem. A clean form of this is \cite[Corollary 3.6]{Szabo:MJM} (taking the group there to be trivial, so that equivariant $\mathcal{Z}$-stability is just $\mathcal{Z}$-stability), which builds on \cite[Theorem 5.4]{SW:APDE}.
head: environment

label: Intro-body:Toms-Winter-Theorem
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{Intro-body:Toms-Winter-Theorem}
    Let $A$ be a simple separable nuclear non-elementary $C^*$-algebra. The following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item $A$ has finite nuclear dimension,
        \item $A$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable,
        \item $A$ has strict comparison (i.e.\ $\operatorname{{Cu}}(A)$ is almost unperforated).
    \end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The equivalence between finite nuclear dimension and $\mathcal{Z}$-stability was established in \cite{winter2012nuclear,Tikuisis:MathAnn,CETWW,CE:APDE}. Moreover, $\mathcal{Z}$-stable $C^*$-algebra have strict comparison by \cite{Rordam:IJM}.
Let $A$ be a simple separable nuclear non-elementary $C^*$-algebra with strict comparison. Then, by \cite{Thiel:arXiv}, $A$ is pure.\footnote{This is \cite[Corollary B]{Thiel:arXiv} in the unital case, and \cite[Theorem E]{Thiel:arXiv} in the non-unital case (as simple $C^*$-algebras have the global Glimm property).} Hence, $A$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable by Theorem~\ref{Intro:pure-implies-Zstable}.

    Let $(\mathcal{M},X)$ be a type II$_1$ factorial tracially complete $C^*$-algebra such that $\mathcal{M}^\omega$ has strict comparison with respect to $X^\omega$ and $\mathcal M^\omega$ has divisible unit.  If $a \in \mathcal M^\omega$ is self-adjoint, then there is a unital embedding $\iota \colon \mathcal R \rightarrow \mathcal M^\omega \cap \{a\}'$.

title: Proof

label: lem:factorial-commutant
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:factorial-commutant}
    Let $(\mathcal{M},X)$ be a  factorial tracially complete $C^*$-algebra such that $\mathcal{M}^\omega$ has strict comparison with respect to $X^\omega$. Given a unital embedding $\iota \colon \mathcal R \subseteq  \mathcal M$, we have that $T(\mathcal{M}^\omega \cap \iota(\mathcal R)') = T(\mathcal{M}^\omega)=X^\omega$ (identified via the restriction map), and so $(\mathcal{M}^\omega \cap \iota(\mathcal R)',X^\omega)$ is a factorial tracially complete $C^*$-algebra.
head: environment

title: Proof
head: environment

label: prop:commutant-cpou
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The tracially complete $C^*$-algebra $(\mathcal{M} \cap \iota(\mathcal R)',X^\omega)$ is factorial by Lemma~\ref{lem:factorial-commutant}. Since $\mathcal R$ is McDuff, for any separable set $S \subseteq \mathcal M^\omega \cap \iota(\mathcal R)'$, we can find a sequence of unital embeddings $j_n\colon \mathcal R\to \iota(\mathcal R)\subseteq \mathcal M^\omega$ which are approximately central. Kirchberg's epsilon test then gives an embedding $j\colon\mathcal R\to \mathcal M^\omega\cap \iota(\mathcal R)'\cap S'$. Hence $(\mathcal M^\omega \cap \iota(\mathcal R)', X^\omega)$ is McDuff.
    The final statement follows from \cite[Proposition~5.22 and Theorem~1.4]{carrion2023tracially}.

label: lem:ETRR02.2
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: cf.\

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $b = a + p + c \in \mathcal M^\omega$.  Define $f, g, h \in C_0((0, 3])$ by
    \begin{equation}
        f(t) \coloneqq \min \{t, 1\}, \quad g(t) \coloneqq \min\{(t-1)_+, 1\}, \quad \text{and} \quad h(t)\coloneqq (t - 2)_+
    \end{equation} 
    for $t \in (0, 3]$.  Then we have $f(b) = a$, $g(b) = p$, and $h(c) = p$ since the $C^*$-algebra generated by $\{a,p,c\}$ is commutative and this holds for complex numbers $a$, $p$, and $c$.  So $a, p, c \in C^*(b)$.

    By Lemma~\ref{lem:central-divide-interval}, there is a unital embedding
    \begin{equation}
        \iota \colon \mathcal R \rightarrow \mathcal M^\omega \cap \{b\}' =\mathcal M^\omega \cap \{a, p, c \}'.
    \end{equation}  Proposition~\ref{prop:commutant-cpou}  then
    implies that $(\mathcal M^\omega \cap \iota(\mathcal R)', X^\omega)$ is a factorial tracially complete $C^*$-algebra with CPoU.
    Applying \cite[Proposition~2.2]{ET:RR0} to this tracially complete $C^*$-algebra (which contains $a,p$ and $c$) gives a positive contraction $q \in \mathcal M^\omega \cap \iota(\mathcal R)'$ satisfying \eqref{eq:rr0-lemma} with $Y$ in place of $X$.  Let $(q_n)_{n=1}^\infty \subseteq \mathcal M$ be a sequence of positive contractions lifting $q$.  Then \eqref{eq:rr0-lemma} holds with $q_n$ in place of $q$ for some $n \in \mathbb N$.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:rr0}
    Let $(\mathcal{M},X)$ be a factorial tracially complete $C^*$-algebra such that $\mathcal{M}^\omega$ has strict comparison with respect to $X^\omega$ and $\mathcal{M}^\omega$ has divisible unit.  Then $\mathcal M$ has real rank zero.

label: lem:RR0StableClassificationOfProjections
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:RR0StableClassificationOfProjections}
    Let $(\mathcal{M},X)$ be a factorial tracially complete $C^*$-algebra with classification of projections.
    Suppose $\mathcal{M}$ has real rank zero.
    Then $(M_n(\mathcal{M}), X_n)$ has classification of projections for every $n \in N$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $n \in \mathbb{N}$. 
    Note that $X_n \cong X$ as topologically affine spaces. We make therefore identify $\operatorname{{Aff}}(X)$ and $\operatorname{{Aff}}(X_n)$.
    Let $f \in \operatorname{{Aff}}(X_n)$ with $0 \leq f \leq 1$. 
    Let $p \in \mathcal{M}$ be a projection with $\tau(p) = f(\tau)$ for all $\tau \in X$.
    Let $p_n = p \oplus \cdots \oplus p \in M_n(\mathcal{M})$ be the $n$-fold direct sum of $p$.
    Then $(\operatorname{{tr}}_n \otimes \tau)(p_n) = \tfrac{1}{n}\cdot n \cdot \tau(p) = f(\tau)$ for all $\tau \in X$.
    Hence, by the definition of $X_n$, we see that $(M_n(\mathcal{M}), X_n)$ has existence of projections.

    Since $\mathcal{M}$ has real rank zero, it follows from \cite[Theorem 2.10]{BrownPedersen:RR0} that $M_n(\mathcal{M})$ also has real rank zero. By \cite[Theorem 1.1]{Zhang:Riesz-Docomposition}, the partially ordered local semigroup $D(M_n(\mathcal{M}))$ of Murray--von Neumann equivalence classes of projections in $M_n(\mathcal{M})$ has the Riesz decomposition property.\footnote{Zhang's result is given for $C^*$-algebras with the property that the self-adjoint elements of finite spectrum are dense in the self-adjoint elements, which is an equivalent formulation of real rank zero (\cite[Theorem 2.6]{BrownPedersen:RR0}).}
     
    Let $p,q \in M_n(\mathcal{M})$ be projections with $\tau(p)\leq\tau(q)$ for all $\tau\in X_n$. Then $[p] \leq n[e_{11} \otimes 1_M]$ in $D(M_n(\mathcal M))$. By the Riesz decomposition property, there exist projections $p_1,\ldots,p_n,\in M_n(\mathcal{M})$ such that  $[p] = \sum_{i=1}^n [p_i]$ and $[p_i] \leq [e_{11} \otimes 1_M]$. Since each $p_i \precsim e_{11} \otimes 1_M$ in $M_n(\mathcal{M})$, we can assume without loss of generality that that each $p_i \in e_{11} \otimes \mathcal{M}$, which we identify with $\mathcal{M}$. Likewise we can write $[q]=\sum_{j=1}^n[q_j]$ for projections $q_j\in\mathcal{M}$. 

    Set $f_i(\tau)=\tau(f_i)$ and $g_j=\tau(q_j)$ for $\tau \in X$. As $(\mathcal{M},X)$ is factorial, $X$ is a Choquet simplex. Therefore, we can apply Riesz decomposition for $\operatorname{{Aff}}(X)$ in the form of Remark \ref{Rem:MoreRieszDecomp} to find $f_{i,j}\in \operatorname{{Aff}}(X)$ with $0\leq f_{i,j}$ and $f_i=\sum_{j=1}^nf_{i,j}$ and $\sum_{i=1}^nf_{i,j}\leq g_j$. Since $(\mathcal{M},X)$ has classification of projections we can find projections $p_{i,j}\in \mathcal{M}$ with $\sum_{j=1}^np_{i,j}=p_i$ and $\tau(p_{i,j})=f_{i,j}(\tau)$ for all $\tau\in X$, as well as projections $q_{i,j}\in\mathcal{M}$ with $\sum_{i=1}^nq_{i,j}\leq q_j$ and $\tau(q_{i,j})=f_{i,j}(\tau)$ for all $\tau\in X$.  Then $p_{i,j}\sim q_{i,j}$ and hence, 
    \begin{equation}
[p]=\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n[p_{i,j}]\leq \sum_{j=1}^n\sum_{i=1}^n[q_{i,j}]\leq [q],
    \end{equation}
    and $M_n(\mathcal{M})$ has classification of projections.

label: prop:MPure
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:MPure}
Let $(\mathcal{M},X)$ be a II$_1$ factorial tracially complete $C^*$-algebra which has classification of projections and real rank zero.  Then $\mathcal{M}$ is pure and has stable rank one as a $C^*$-algebra.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: From Lemma~\ref{lem:RR0StableClassificationOfProjections}, we see that $V(\mathcal{M})\cong \operatorname{{Aff}} T(X)_+$ as ordered semigroups, so pureness follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:ETpure}.  Also the computation of $V(\mathcal M)$ implies $\mathcal M$ has cancellation of projections, so it has stable rank one by Proposition~\ref{prop:RR0CancellationSR1}.

label: prop:dense-subalgebra
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:dense-subalgebra}
	Let $A$ be a $C^*$-algebra, $X \subseteq T(A)$ be a compact convex subset, and $\iota \colon A \rightarrow \overline{A}{}^{X}$ denote the canonical inclusion. Let $a, b \in A_+$. Then $a \precsim_X b$ in $A$ if and only if $\iota(a) \precsim_X \iota(b)$ in $\overline{A}{}^{X}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $a, b \in A_+$. 
    Since $\iota$ is a $\|\cdot\|_{2,X}$-preserving $^*$-homomorphism, it is clear that $a \precsim_X b$ in $A$ implies $\iota(a) \precsim_X \iota(b)$.
    
    Suppose $\iota(a) \precsim_X \iota(b)$ and $\epsilon > 0$.  Let $\bar v \in \overline{A}{}^{X}$ be such that $\| \bar v^* \iota(b) \bar v - a \|_{2, X} < \epsilon$.
	Using the tracially complete analogue of Kaplansky's density theorem (\cite[Proposition~3.28]{carrion2023tracially}),  there is $v \in A$ with $\|v\| \leq \|\bar v\|$ such that $\|\iota(v) - \bar v\|_{2, X} < \epsilon/ (\|b\| \|v\| + 1)$.  Then $\|v^* b v - a \|_{2, X} < 3 \epsilon$, so $a \precsim_X b$.

label: PurenessThm-body
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
It is clear that \ref{it:Pureness.3-body} implies \ref{it:Pureness.1-body}.
    
    Suppose \ref{it:Pureness.1-body} holds.  Then by Theorem~\ref{Thm:StrictComparisonEquivalences}, $\mathcal M^\omega$ has strict comparison with respect to $X^\omega$.   Fix $k \in \mathbb N$.  Since approximately constant rank functions occur in $\mathcal M$, there are $n \in \mathbb N$ and $a \in \mathcal M_n(A)_+$ be such that
    \begin{equation}
        \frac1{k+1}< d_\tau(a) < \frac1k, \quad \tau \in X,  
    \end{equation}
    and hence also for $\tau \in X^\omega$, so strict comparison implies $ka \leq [1_{\mathcal M^\omega}] \leq (k +1) [a]$, and hence $[1_{\mathcal M^\omega}]$ is approximately divisible in $\mathcal M^\omega$.  Applying Proposition~\ref{prop:sc_divisible_tracial_ultra} and using Kirchberg's epsilon test, we get exact divisibility of $1_{\mathcal{M}^\omega}$.  Then $(\mathcal M, X)$ has classification of projections by Theorem~\ref{thm:classif-proj} and 
    $\mathcal M$ has real rank zero by Theorem~\ref{thm:rr0}.  So \ref{it:Pureness.4-body} holds.  

    Assuming \ref{it:Pureness.4-body}, Theorem~\ref{Class:FD} implies $\mathcal M$ has classification of finite-dimensional subalgebras and hence the unit is divisible, and Proposition~\ref{prop:rr0-comparison} implies $\mathcal M$ has strict comparison with respect to $X$. This shows \ref{it:Pureness.3-body}.

    Now assume $(\mathcal M, X)$ satisfies \ref{it:Pureness.1-body}, \ref{it:Pureness.3-body} and \ref{it:Pureness.4-body}.  It follows from \ref{it:Pureness.4-body} and Proposition~\ref{prop:MPure} that $\mathcal M$ is pure and has stable rank one.  By \ref{it:Pureness.3-body} and Proposition~\ref{prop:computing-traces}, $T(\mathcal M) = X$.

label: cor:regular
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The tracial completion $(\overline{A}{}^{T(A)}, T(A))$ is a factorial tracially complete $C^*$-algebra by \cite[Proposition~3.23(iv)]{carrion2023tracially}, and the divisibility condition on $A$ readily implies it is type II$_1$.  Since the tracial ultrapower of $(\overline{A}{}^{T(A)}, T(A))$ is $(A^\omega, \overline{T_\omega(A)})$, it suffices to prove the second statement.
    
    Suppose $(\mathcal M, X)$ is regular.  Then $(\mathcal M^\omega, X^\omega)$ has approximately constant rank functions (realised by the same positive elements from matrices over $\mathcal M$), and by Theorem~\ref{Thm:StrictComparisonEquivalences}, $(\mathcal M^\omega, X^\omega)$ has strict $(2, X^\omega)$-comparison.  So $(\mathcal M^\omega, X^\omega)$ is regular.
    
    Conversely, suppose $(\mathcal M^\omega, X^\omega)$ is regular. Then, by Theorem~\ref{Thm:StrictComparisonEquivalences}, $(\mathcal M, X)$ has strict $(2, X)$-comparison, and by lifting positive matrices over $\mathcal M^\omega$ to sequences of positive matrices over $\mathcal M$, we see that $\mathcal M$ has approximately constant rank functions since $\mathcal M^\omega$ does.
